verdict.rationale: Snoozing is clearly documented: a conversation is hidden until a set time and then returns to the Inbox, triggered by swipe or the ⌘/Ctrl+K command bar. The 'resurface if nobody replies' half is only approximated by multi-step rules that wait and act on unanswered emails (label, notify, reassign), not by a documented per-thread follow-up reminder that brings the conversation back. missing for 10: a native per-conversation 'remind me if no reply' option that resurfaces the thread, documentation that snooze can be conditional on replies, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a power-user, I can snooze conversations and set follow-up reminders that resurface a thread if nobody replies

citations.quote: Snoozing temporarily hides a conversation until a specific time, then brings it back to your Inbox.
You can also snooze by swiping a conversation (configurable in Settings > Preferences > Swipes), or by opening the command bar with ⌘/Ctrl + K and typing "snooze".
Rules can now run in steps over time. Each step waits, checks its own conditions, then acts on the same conversation.
Escalate unanswered support emails: label at 24 hrs, notify the lead at 48, reassign at 72.
SLA alerts and follow-up sequences now fit in one rule instead of several.
